topic: Country with the most proven crude oil reserves: Venezuela — 303.2 billion barrels (OPEC ASB 2025, end-2024), ≈ 19 % of the world's 1,567 billion; Saudi Arabia 267.2 billion second; Iran, Canada, Iraq follow; Russia ≈ 80 billion; nearly all of Venezuela's reserves are extra-heavy crude in the Orinoco Belt; Venezuelan output ≈ 0.9–1.0 million b/d ≈ 1 % of world supply (~103 million b/d)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Saudi Arabia has the most oil in the world.
myths.reality: Saudi Arabia produces more, but Venezuela holds the most proven reserves — 303 billion barrels against Saudi Arabia's 267 billion (OPEC 2025).

opec_asb.title: Annual Statistical Bulletin 2025 — proven crude oil reserves (end-2024)
opec_asb.notes: Venezuela 303.221 billion barrels (world's most); Saudi Arabia 267.2; world total ≈ 1,567 billion

eia_venezuela.title: Country analysis — Venezuela
eia_venezuela.notes: holds the world's most proven crude reserves, mostly extra-heavy crude in the Orinoco Belt; production fell to under 1 million b/d from ~3 million in the late 1990s

eia_world.title: Short-Term Energy Outlook — world liquid fuels production
eia_world.notes: world petroleum and liquids production ≈ 103 million b/d in 2025 — Venezuela's ~0.9–1.0 million b/d is about 1 %

opec_prod.title: Monthly Oil Market Report — crude production by secondary sources
opec_prod.notes: Venezuela crude output ≈ 0.9–1.0 million b/d in 2025

reuters_ven.title: Venezuela oil output and exports (2025 coverage)
reuters_ven.notes: output around 0.9–1.1 million b/d against ~103 million b/d global liquids supply — roughly 1 %

britannica_orinoco.title: Orinoco Belt / Venezuela — resources
britannica_orinoco.notes: the Orinoco Belt (Faja del Orinoco), a strip north of the lower Orinoco River, holds one of the world's great accumulations of extra-heavy crude and bitumen

wiki_reserves.title: List of countries by proven oil reserves
wiki_reserves.notes: Venezuela 303 bn, Saudi Arabia 267 bn, Iran 209 bn, Canada 163 bn, Iraq 145 bn; Russia ≈ 80 bn (8th)
